correctness.rationale: Taking coordinate moduli bounds the numerical-range quadratic form by the real adjacency Rayleigh quotient, and equality holds at a positive Perron vector, also for the connected path r=0. Reflection and the interior recurrence give positive cosine/cosh vectors and the two endpoint equations. The trigonometric ratio decreases from 1 to 0 on the stated interval. The hyperbolic ratio is cosh η+tanh((n−1)η/2)sinh η, increasing in η and n. For r<1 the phase equation nθ+2 arctan(((1+r)/(1−r))tan(θ/2))=π yields strict monotonicity and θ=π/(n+(1+r)/(1−r))+O_r(n^−4). For r>1 the exponential variable q satisfies q−r=(rq−1)q^−n; the row-sum bound keeps q bounded, so q−r=O_r(r^−n), and replacing q by r on the right costs O_r(nr^−2n). Expanding (q+q^−1)/2 yields the claimed coefficient. After rescaling the exact monotone boundary equations by n, compact root bracketing gives the trigonometric and hyperbolic limits; continuity at a=0 follows from the small-root quadratic forms. The source checker was inspected, not executed. This does not assume fixed-r error bounds are uniform near r=1.

originality.rationale: Grudsky–Maximenko–Soto-González (2020), arXiv:2009.01401, study exactly the relevant matrix up to the affine change A_{r,n}=2I−B_n(r), not merely a similar cycle Laplacian. Their exact weak and strong characteristic equations specialize to the identical scalar equations for the lowest eigenvalue. The signed crossover is a direct rescaling of these exact prior equations, not an inference from their nonuniform fixed-strength error estimates. The previously displayed exponential order and other finite-size statements or leading coefficients also follow by elementary expansion or monotonicity of the same equations. No explicit statement of the double-scaled limit is attributed to that paper.
